attacks.claim: The performance table shows every invocation regressing badly (--version 0.11s→1.94s, lint-staged 0.38s→2.31s, cache-hit run 0.21s→2.02s), yet the text dismisses this as 'negligible' because cold builds improve. Pre-commit hooks run lint-staged on every commit, so each commit gets ~6x slower; this is a daily developer-facing regression that the artifact misrepresents.
attacks.evidence: "Discovery is a fixed per-invocation cost and becomes negligible relative to real build work" vs. table: "tasq lint-staged (3 staged files) | 0.38 s | 2.31 s"

attacks.claim: The discovery glob walks `**/node_modules/**/package.json` from root, which enumerates every nested package.json across all 2,430 installed packages on each invocation. The claimed 'cold build 46.1s vs 48.7s improvement' is attributed to caching, but the cache-hit path is the one that regressed, so the caching benefit is not demonstrated for the common path.
attacks.evidence: "for await (const pkgJson of glob("**/node_modules/**/package.json", { cwd: root }))"

attacks.claim: Auto-discovery loads any installed package carrying the `tasq-plugin` keyword with no allowlist, signature check, or trust prompt. Any transitive dependency (or a typosquat/compromised package) can inject code that runs on every `tasq run`, `lint-staged`, and pre-commit hook, which the docs tell users to wire into git and CI. The artifact does not describe any trust boundary for plugins.
attacks.evidence: "Any installed package with the `tasq-plugin` keyword is picked up automatically." / "loads the ones whose `keywords` include `tasq-plugin`"

attacks.claim: Discovery is also a supply-chain amplifier: publishing a package with the keyword is enough for code to be loaded in every tasq user's workspace. The 'no postinstall' claim does not cover this, since the loaded plugin code runs at tasq invocation time.
attacks.evidence: "No `postinstall` scripts in tasq or its dependencies."

attacks.claim: The rollback plan is incomplete for a breaking major. Users who migrated to 3.0.0 via tasq-migrate have rewritten configs and CJS-to-ESM changes; re-pointing `latest` to 2.9.4 does not revert their repos. Also `npm dist-tag add` does not unpublish; users who already installed 3.0.0 remain on it until they change ranges, and the 7-day `next` soak is the only pre-promotion gate.
attacks.evidence: "re-point `latest` to `2.9.4` (`npm dist-tag add tasq@2.9.4 latest`) and publish a fix as 3.0.1."

attacks.claim: Breaking-change table says `tasq-migrate` 'installs nothing new' and that 2 of 40 repos needed manual edits, but the Yarn PnP projects that failed are exactly the monorepo style where the new node_modules walk is most fragile (PnP has no node_modules tree). Discovery silently finds zero plugins there, so plugins stop loading with no error.

Discovery runs on every invocation, including `tasq watch` restarts, with no caching of the plugin list and no error handling shown for unreadable or malformed package.json; a single bad package.json in node_modules throws from JSON.parse and aborts the command for all users.
Compute cost of re-walking node_modules on every hook/CI invocation is not quantified in CI minutes terms, though CI-heavy users will feel the 2s-per-call overhead.

Performance claims are based on a single reference machine (M2 MacBook Air, warm cache) and rc.2 only; no Linux or cold-disk CI numbers are provided even though CI is a documented primary use case, and the 'under 50 ms task time' cache claim has no measurement.
attacks.evidence: "repeated `tasq run build` with unchanged inputs completes in under 50 ms of task time"

attacks.claim: No accessibility concern is evident in the release artifact; the pretty reporter change is output formatting and no screen-reader or contrast impact is described.
The pretty lint-staged reporter output change is described only as 'grouped output' with no sample, so visible format changes for users parsing output are unspecified.
Discovery reads package.json contents across all installed packages; no personal data collection is described, so no concrete privacy failure is evident.
Publishing via npm only with no mirror or alternative registry plan; no concrete lock-in failure is evidenced for an MIT CLI.

Discovery cost scales with installed package count; at 10x (24k packages) or in large monorepos the per-invocation glob cost grows linearly and runs before argument parsing, so even `--version` scales with dependency count.
attacks.evidence: "Discovery runs before argument parsing so that plugins can register subcommands."

attacks.claim: License scan is claimed clean; no concrete compliance failure is evident.

Every hook and CI invocation pays a roughly 1.5 to 2 second penalty on the reference repo, a friction regression users will notice on each commit and make, with no opt-out or cache of the plugin list described.
Discovery glob pattern `**/node_modules/**/package.json` is untested for nested workspace layouts beyond the one reference repo; coupling to node_modules layout is a hidden dependency.
The rc.2 smoke test covered only the top 15 community plugins; the wider plugin ecosystem, including plugins that rely on the removed `plugins` array, is not checked.
attacks.evidence: "Smoke test of top 15 community plugins under auto-discovery: all load and register subcommands."
